title: Expand icon support with an open-source icon set like iconoir or remixicon out of the box
body: ### Checklist - [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests. - [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue. ### Summary I have been building Enterprise grade platforms using Streamlit (mostly as a UI + web app delivery framework for Python, plus added benefits of chart support) and I had a good experience with the limitation of Streamlit currently, especially for the app appearance (I opened a few other cosmetic issues ✨ ). Emojis are less and less suited as the only option as Streamlit becomes more and more appealing to build web apps in. Since `st.image()` does not support SVG files well, I had some limited success hacking together some HTML to insert a text field with the icon, but it won't work where I'd like it to (on widget titles, on sidebar pages etc.) ### Why? On limitation which really struck me was the lack of non-emoji icons. The main negative about emojis, is that for some cases it may not look professional enough, they may not look the same on every os (Win 11 supports more emojis than Win10 for example, and in my case some visual glitches on the customer end); but mostly for me it's the **lack of diversity**. There's almost a point everyday in my work where I struggle with finding an emoji that fit, so whilst I love them I do believe Streamlit is at a point of maturity where it's time to support an open-source, complete, neutral and extensive icon set . This also fits the Streamlit milestone this year to improve customization : this would come without much foreseeable CSS/HTML hackery, tech debt or impairement to current functionality. ### How? The emphasis of addressing this concern should be to rely on core Streamlit values: - Choose 1 set, that has a lot of options and will look good at any case. Icon sets like [iconoir](https://iconoir.com/) , [RemixIcon](https://remixicon.com/) contain thousands of ready to use icons or any other set. - Icons can be used just like emojis today are with a specific syntax in-line of any text field (i.e. _emoji_:`: face:` , _icon_: `:::` - or whatever syntax is most parsable). This will make it very convenient for everyone to adopt, and once support is built it'll scale well. - Make it like fonts served by Streamlit locally (or by Streamlit Cloud), in case of air gapped installations. - Update dependency for whatever icon set is chose with every streamlit update, since new icons are added or updated frequently (new vendor icons, technologies etc.) ### Additional Context

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Listing here a few notable icon library that could be options, if interested by such feature folks can react to show preference toward any particular one.

> At the moment, I believe that Material Icons may be the most suited with strong vendor support and the most icons out of any high quality libraries I could find (apart from font awesome, see below).

| 👉 Regarding [Font Awesome](https://fontawesome.com/)|
|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| Font Awesome is an icon library with more than 26000 icons. No other libraries come close to it in term of raw numbers. It has a [custom license](https://github.com/FortAwesome/Font-Awesome/blob/6.x/LICENSE.txt), but it mostly takes the same terms as a MIT license, requiring attribution. It also has a commercial interest in the form of a pro service. Finally, those 26k+ icons include styling variant (thin, duotone etc.) which are all payed options; the actual count available to Streamlit would be much smaller. For all those reasons, to de-risk continued support I propose to scope it out of this feature request, and build a stronger icon support for Streamlit with an active open-source library with less commercial interest around it. |

_Criteria of selection:_
- More than a few hundreds icons to address most use cases
- Strictly open source, with a license which allows commercial reuse
- Active and supported project
- All icons must have been designed by the project (no mix of multiple libraries)
- "Modern" styling (I did not further selection apart from filtering what fits the general aesthetic of streamlit).


| Reaction | Library| License| Icons |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| 👀 | [Material Symbols](https://fonts.google.com/icons) | Apache License 2.0 | 3,031 |
| 🎉 | [Remix Icons](https://remixicon.com/)| Apache License 2.0 | 2537 |
| 🚀 | [Iconoir](https://iconoir.com/) | MIT License | 1368 |
| ❤️ | [Phosphor Icons](https://phosphoricons.com/) | MIT License | 1248 |

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Thanks for all the detail, that's super cool! We currently don't have any plans to support non-emoji icons but I'm not completely opposed to it / can see that there are cases where "normal" icons work better. If you (or anyone else) has specific cases where emojis don't work well, please add them as comments here! That will help us assess the priority and figure out what's the best solution if we want to support this in the future.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Btw `st.image` should work with SVG images afaik. If there are issues, feel free to open a bug report.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> Thanks for all the detail, that's super cool! We currently don't have any plans to support non-emoji icons but I'm not completely opposed to it / can see that there are cases where "normal" icons work better. If you (or anyone else) has specific cases where emojis don't work well, please add them as comments here! That will help us assess the priority and figure out what's the best solution if we want to support this in the future.

I can speak from my end : design multi page CRUD apps in Streamlit for cyberdefence teams, with a bunch of editing options, automation, feedback etc. It has been feedback to multiple time by clients that they actively dislike emojis. From the dev angle, when I need a graphic for specific concept, emojis fall more and more flat; especially since the topics I deal with are very precise. What emoji fits Detection Rule ? Playbook ? Incident Response ? EC2 Instance ? Log Forwarding ? I can find some things as abstraction, but it doesn't look as nice or explicit as  professionally designed icons; and with a larger lib at my fingertips I can more adequately find either exactly what I need, or a close second.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> Btw `st.image` should work with SVG images afaik. If there are issues, feel free to open a bug report.

It really doesn't ! Width parameter is completely broken, and the rendeing often completely fails even with the official streamlit svg. Some SVG work, but can't be resized without editing the svg,

I'll try to compile a more comprehensive report and bug issue.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: +1. Really miss better icons selection. One of the reasons I started using Streamlit options menu extra component - is for icons. Would love to see better icons support for Streamlit components, maybe even direct svg/image for icons (buttons, menu items).

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: I second what everyone else reported in this issue. Emojis are confusing more often than not since UX needs to be guided by images sometimes. Also, we need to consider that emojis come in colors, which may not fit well with the application color coding, contributing to give the feeling that an app isn't polished as it should. I +1 the integration of FontAwesome since it has a vast library of icons.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: We have built and deployed an enterprise-grade app, and I've had feedback that the emojis lack professionalism and don't convey the nuances of the product feature that increase user recognition. It would be fantastic to be able to integrate icon sets not only in the main web page, but also in the multi-page navigation feature so that users can instantly recognise which page does what.

comments.body: Agreed here! , also changing the icon and name in an embedded link (like if a user sends a slack message or text message with app link ) it shows up with default streamlit crown and "Streamlit" , I firmly believe these little details will make streamlit a enticing framework for app development

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
Is there a reason why you don’t want to do something like `st.use_iconlib(name/path)`? This would allow people to have their custom icon-set which fits their specific requirements (eg. if you want to have an icon for some technology you’re using). You could have some default (idk, I guess one of the ones reporter proposed above) so it isn’t necessary to use this function.
I’m new here, so please tell me if this is violating any idea/guideline of streamlit.

comments.author: participant8
comments.body: This is now supported for [Material Symbols](https://fonts.google.com/icons) via `icon=":<nick>/<icon>:"` on most commands that support icons. We'll be adding it soon for st.page_link and the upcoming st.navigation for side navigation.
